sections.label: QC inspections statutory requirement
sections.summary: Amendments make QC inspections of AEs a statutory requirement, letting ACRA inspect all AEs, compel remediation of lapses and impose sanctions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The first set of amendments therefore seeks to make QC inspections of AEs a statutory requirement under the Accountants Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will allow ACRA to conduct inspections on all AEs and compel AEs to remediate lapses uncovered during the QC inspections, including imposing sanctions where necessary.

sections.label: AML/CFT inspection powers
sections.summary: Amendments give ACRA powers to inspect compliance with AML/CFT requirements and sanction PAs and AEs that fail to comply.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The second set of amendments give ACRA powers to conduct inspections for compliance with AML/CFT requirements and to impose sanctions on PAs and AEs if they fail to comply with these requirements.

sections.label: Tiered assessment framework
sections.summary: The third amendment revises the assessment framework from a pass-fail regime to a tiered regime.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The third amendment thus revises the assessment framework from a pass-fail regime to a tiered regime.

sections.label: Disclosure of inspection findings
sections.summary: PAOC may require a PA graded not satisfactory to disclose engagement-level inspection findings to the audited entity, or share them directly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Under this amendment, the PAOC will be empowered to require a PA with a "not satisfactory" grading for that particular engagement-level inspection to disclose the inspection findings to the audited entity.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: If the PA fails to comply, the PAOC can share the inspection findings on the PAs' audit engagement with the audited entity directly.

sections.label: Related amendments and foreign alignment
sections.summary: Disclosure to audited entities aligns with Canada, Australia and Malaysia; the Bill also covers fees, appeals, orders and professional standards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The disclosure of inspection findings on the PAs' audit engagements to the audited entity is in line with the requirements in Canada, Australia and Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Besides the four key sets of amendments, the Bill also provides for related amendments, such as the prescription of fees, laying out processes relating to appeals and meting out of orders, as well as empowering the PAOC to prescribe professional standards for PAs and AEs.

sections.label: Support for Accountants Act Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill amending the Accountants Act to enhance audit regulation and compliance by public accountants and accounting entities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This is crucial in engendering trust and confidence in the quality of audited financial statements and ultimately, in the PAs and AEs themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I support this Bill which proposes to amend the Accountants Act to enhance the audit regulatory regime and introduce measures for better compliance with professional requirements and standards by both public accountants and accounting entities.

sections.label: Support for small audit practices
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Government can help small and medium-sized audit practices facing limited resources and an audit professional shortage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The smaller firms with limited resources are likely to have lesser time, knowledge and most importantly, the resources to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill came at a time when there is a severe shortage of audit professionals in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While I believe members of the profession recognise the need for emphasis on quality, the challenges they face should be acknowledged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to raise the question of how the Government can help the profession, especially the small and medium-sized audit practices, that is, the SMPs.

sections.label: Appointment of entity reviewers
sections.summary: New section 38E lets the oversight committee appoint suitably qualified employees or individuals as entity reviewers for quality control or AML/CFT reviews.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new section 38E empowers the oversight committee to appoint any employee of the authority or any other individual who is suitably qualified as entity reviewers to carry out a review of quality control standards or AML/CFT requirements or both.

sections.label: Subsidies for adapting to changes
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will provide subsidies during the easing-in period to help PAs and AEs adapt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Government provide subsidies as part of the easing-in period to help PAs and AEs to adapt to the changes?

sections.label: Remediation timeframe and escalation
sections.summary: The speaker asks if there is a designated remediation timeframe before sanctions and a clear escalation mechanism for non-remediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourthly, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, will there be a designated timeframe for remediation of lapses before sanctions are imposed?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If adequate remediation efforts are not met within the time limit for AEs and PAs which are deemed to be "Need Improvement" or "Unsatisfactory", is there a clear escalation mechanism in place for non-remediation and sanctions?

sections.label: Leeway for innovation and compliance
sections.summary: The speaker asks how leeway can be granted for AEs to experiment with innovations and productivity measures while safeguarding compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Even as we tighten the framework to promote quality auditing, how can we also grant leeway to facilitate the experimentation of new innovations and productivity measures amongst AEs, yet safeguard compliance?

sections.label: Local talent and reasonable excuse
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Singaporean students join accounting and asks the Minister for examples of a reasonable excuse under these sections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also hope that more of our Singaporean students, especially those listening in, will be attracted to accounting as a profession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is amidst our hunt for local talent to keep Singapore running, knowing the critical role that they will play.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Having good local talent, coupled with a strong legislative framework buttressed by this Bill, will, in turn, translate into more efficient and secure investment decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This also equates to higher returns and greater investor confidence, thereby entrenching Singapore's position as a global financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide examples to explain what constitutes a reasonable excuse under these sections?

sections.label: Sub-committee further investigations
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether and how the Sub-committee and the Committee can conduct further investigations to make a more informed decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share whether and how the Sub-committee and the Committee can conduct further investigations so they can make a more informed decision?

sections.label: Oversight Committee written decisions
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether the Oversight Committee will as a matter of course provide a written decision on the basis for its orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To ensure that there is meaningful access to review by the Court, can the Minister share if the Oversight Committee will, as a matter of course, provide a written decision on the basis for its orders?

sections.label: Redaction of confidential information
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether MOF and ACRA will generally consent to redaction of confidential information if accounting entities apply to the Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To provide greater assurance to accounting entities, can the Minister share if MOF and ACRA will generally consent to the redaction of confidential information if such an application is made by the accounting entities to the Court?

sections.label: ACRA risk-based QC inspections
sections.summary: ACRA's QC inspections will take a risk-based approach to avoid unnecessary inspection and compliance burden for AEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To Mr Yip Hon Weng's question on how the Government would help AEs manage cost of compliance, ACRA's QC inspections will take a risk-based approach to avoid unnecessary inspection and compliance burden.

sections.label: Fee caps for AE inspections
sections.summary: ACRA will set fee caps for inspections of AEs in the non-PIE segment, calibrated to be manageable for SMPs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To ensure cost of compliance remains reasonable, ACRA will be setting fee caps for inspections of AEs in the non-PIE segment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The fee caps will be calibrated to ensure that they will be manageable for SMPs.

sections.label: Remedial orders and sanctions
sections.summary: Orders will primarily be remedial if non-compliance is not too severe, but sanctions may be necessary for very severe and recurring non-compliances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If areas of non-compliance are not too severe, orders imposed on the PAs and AEs will primarily be remedial in nature.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, for very severe and recurring non-compliances, sanctions may be necessary to protect public interest and send a strong deterrent message in addition to the remedial orders.

sections.label: PA continuing professional education hours
sections.summary: PAs must maintain at least 120 continuing professional education hours over a rolling three-year period, and from 1 January 2023 ACRA will include Information Technology as a core expertise area requiring minimum training hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To encourage our PAs to upskill, we currently require all PAs to maintain at least 120 continuing professional education hours over a rolling three-year period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: From 1 January 2023, ACRA will also include Information Technology as a core expertise area that PAs would need to obtain a minimum number of training hours in.

sections.label: Support schemes and COMPASS shortage list
sections.summary: Schemes such as the Productivity Solutions Grant support AEs, and Mr Wee requested audit professionals be included in MOM's COMPASS Shortage Occupation List, which awards bonus points for Employment Pass applications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: There are several schemes to support AEs to do so, such as the Productivity Solutions Grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I note Mr Wee's request for audit professionals to be included in MOM's COMPASS Shortage Occupation List (SOL).

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The SOL awards bonus points under the COMPASS for employment, pass for Employment Pass (EP) applications, filling occupations requiring highly specialised skills that are in shortage in our local workforce.
